theoretical_axes.information_axis: pre-commitment cue reliability / predictive connectivity / environmental predictability
theoretical_axes.recourse_axis: post-commitment ability to alter timing, pace, stopover use, route, or later phenological schedule
theoretical_axes.key_boundary: predictability before error and correction after error are distinct quantities; neither may be substituted for the other

result.interpretation: stronger detrended pre-outcome predictive connectivity associated with smaller arrival-greenup mismatch

information_axis.boundary: pooled directional support; dependence-aware intervals prevent universal species-independent claim

information_axis.interpretation: long-distance migrants are less temperature-responsive than short-distance migrants
information_axis.boundary: migration distance is not identical to information distance and is not D_eff

information_axis.source: Kölzsch et al. 2015 J Anim Ecol 84:272-283
information_axis.result: arrival timing was closer to local spring onset where consecutive-stopover phenology predictability was higher
information_axis.boundary: published predictability is route-level information; not retained actionability r

recourse_axis.interpretation: signed recourse: ahead animals decelerate / wait more; behind animals accelerate / shorten stopovers
recourse_axis.boundary: does not identify natural D_eff or reduced-form r

recourse_axis.interpretation: incoming phase error is transformed across route stages; actuator architecture includes stopover and overtaking
recourse_axis.boundary: lambda is a phase-retention response coordinate, not actionability r

recourse_axis.interpretation: earlier initial departure can be absorbed by longer later stopover

recourse_axis.result: flowering/activity duration can buffer overlap loss in local systems
recourse_axis.boundary: taxon identity cannot be used as a recourse proxy

cross_axis_tests.design: preregistered historical predictive-connectivity x incoming-phase interaction
cross_axis_tests.prediction: higher predictive connectivity -> stronger phase correction -> lower retention
cross_axis_tests.interpretation: pre-commitment information is not a portable amplifier of post-error correction
higher environmental predictability did not imply stronger realized correction
cross_axis_tests.boundary: small and non-independent; descriptive boundary evidence, not a general negative relationship

cross_axis_tests.design: preregistered preoutcome cue-linked downstream transit-compression screen
cross_axis_tests.prediction: warmer local cues should predict shorter downstream transit more strongly where historical predictive connectivity to Bylot is higher
cross_axis_tests.role: closest prospective same-system bridge between information and downstream compensation

supported: information availability and post-commitment correction are both empirically measurable in natural systems
the two axes are not interchangeable
better pre-commitment predictability does not imply universally stronger post-error correction
seasonal timing can be stabilized through different mixtures of prediction and downstream correction
not_supported: predictive connectivity is equivalent to phase-correction gain
phase-retention lambda is equivalent to reduced-form actionability r
migration distance is equivalent to information quality q
a natural estimate of the continuous-time optimal commitment condition
synthesis.current_best_general_statement: seasonal tracking has at least two separable control channels: prediction before commitment and correction after mismatch; their relative contributions vary among routes and systems
synthesis.current_direct_test_bottleneck: one system must independently calibrate q(t), biological actionability/recourse, waiting cost, and commitment behavior on a common scale
